questions.q: What is the correct order of the DHCP process?
A PC shows the address 169.254.12.7. What does this usually mean?
options: It received an address from the DHCP server
It could not reach a DHCP server and gave itself an address
It is using a public address
It is using the loopback address
questions.explain: 169.254.0.0/16 is used for automatic private addressing (APIPA) when DHCP fails.

questions.q: Which port does DNS normally use?
questions.explain: DNS uses port 53 (UDP normally, TCP for large answers and zone transfers). Port 67 is DHCP, 80 is HTTP and 443 is HTTPS.

questions.q: Which DNS record maps a name to an IPv4 address?
questions.explain: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address. AAAA is for IPv6, MX points to mail servers and PTR is for reverse lookups.

questions.q: ping 8.8.8.8 works, but ping www.example.com fails. What is the most likely problem?
options: The router is out of power
questions.explain: The path to the Internet works, because pinging an IP address succeeds. Only the translation of the name into an address fails.

options: Many private hosts to share one public IP address by using different port numbers
A device to get an address automatically
Names to be translated into addresses
VLANs to talk to each other
questions.explain: PAT (NAT overload) keeps a translation table with port numbers so that many inside devices can share a single public address.

questions.q: Which keyword turns NAT into PAT in a Cisco ip nat inside source command?
What does the DHCP lease time define?
options: How long a device may keep its address before it must renew it
How fast the DHCP server replies
The maximum number of devices on the network
How long a DNS answer stays in the cache
questions.explain: A lease is a temporary loan of an address. The device renews it before it expires, otherwise the address returns to the pool.
